one_liner: C++ multiprecision integer/rational/float types over GMP with inline small-value storage; 4-8x faster than raw GMP on 1-limb operands.
what_it_does: mp++ provides integer<SSize>, rational<SSize>, real (MPFR), complex (MPC), real128 and complex128 types with operator overloading and modern C++ idioms. integer<SSize> is a value-semantic replacement for mpz_t / Boost gmp_int; it exposes get_mpz_t() and a read-only mpz_view, so existing GMP calls keep working. It is a compiled library (CMake) rather than header-only.
how_it_is_fast: Small-buffer (small-value) optimisation: values up to SSize 64-bit limbs live inline in the object with no heap allocation, and only spill to a GMP mpz_t when they grow past SSize. Hand-written primitives for SSize 1 and 2 (add, mul, addmul, div, shift, gcd) avoid GMP's general-purpose call and allocation overhead on tiny operands.
when_to_use: Computer algebra / polynomial coefficient arithmetic where most integers fit in 64 or 128 bits but must not overflow.
Large vectors of mostly-small arbitrary-precision integers (dot products, multiply-add, division, sort) where GMP's per-object heap allocation dominates.
You want a modern C++ wrapper over GMP/MPFR/MPC with one consistent API, including arbitrary-precision special functions via FLINT/Arb.
Code that must interoperate with existing mpz_t-based libraries without copying.
when_not_to_use: Large operands (many limbs): arithmetic defers to GMP, so expect no speedup and a small wrapper cost.
You need fixed-width wide integers (uint256/uint512): explicitly a non-goal; use Boost.Multiprecision fixed cpp_int.
Dependency-free or header-only builds: GMP is mandatory and the library is built with CMake.
Projects needing an actively maintained dependency: last commit 2024-12-10 (2.0.0).

integration.dependencies: GMP 5+ (required); optional MPFR 3+, GNU MPC, FLINT 3+, libquadmath, Boost (serialization/benchmarks), fmt 6.2+
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (uses C++14/17/20 features when available), CMake 3.12; tested on GCC, Clang, MSVC
integration.platforms: Linux, Windows, macOS, FreeBSD; x86 and ARM
integration.thread_safety: not documented (docs only note thread_local performance issues on MinGW and older Xcode)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — value type with mpz_t interop (get_mpz_t, mpz_view, mpz_t constructors), but code using raw mpz_* calls must be rewritten to use the class API to benefit

gotchas: Choice of SSize is a compile-time tradeoff: larger SSize bloats every object; optimised fast paths exist only for SSize 1 and 2.
Promotion to dynamic storage is automatic but demotion back to static storage requires an explicit demote() call.
mpz_view references internal data and is invalidated by modifying the integer; assigning from an aliasing mpz_t is not allowed.
Binary serialization format is platform-specific, not for long-term storage.
verified_claims_summary: First-party mp++ 2.0.0 benchmark page compares integer<1>/<2> to GMP (via Boost gmp_int), Boost cpp_int, FLINT fmpzxx and native ints on 3e7-element vectors: on 1-limb unsigned values mp++ is ~4x faster than GMP for dot product, >7x for multiply-add and ~8x for division (FLINT similar on division). Compiler, flags and CPU are not stated.
status_note: Stale since mp++ 2.0.0 (2024-12-10) with 9 open issues, but MPL-2.0, on conda-forge and mature enough to use as a dependency.
